6. Each tool gets its best configuration

The fairness rule: no tool is run with a capability disabled that another tool is given, and no tool is
given a configuration tuned on a result. What "best" means for each, with the commands taken from
Best configuration, and the command that proves it
the built CLI, offline, on the pinned commit, every built-in detector, cache bypassed, no severity gate, no narrowing:

8. Binding rules for the run and for publishing

This page is amended only by a dated entry that states whether the amendment was made after seeing a
result; a measure changed after a run forces a fresh run of both tools, published together.

Both tools run on the same checkout at the same commit, in the same working tree, and the commit is
in the result file.
Every disagreement is published as its own row with the evidence link, as

already does for Renovate. Aggregate claims
without the row table are rejected.

Losses are published with the same detail as wins; the report where the other tool found more is
the headline of the run that produced it.

No result changes a registry rule, a threshold, a floor, or an allowlist entry as part of the run
(
: an entry may never be added or raised to make something pass).
gates every run's pull request, and

is not part of it
— it needs the network, so a run records how it was executed and whether the cache was warm.
9. Reproducing the tables, and the method

One command rebuilds every committed comparison table from the committed inputs and compares it with
the published known result. It runs from a clean checkout with no network, no repository code, and no
clock:

The command prints the pinned versions and the headline counts, then checks every generated file and
the known result byte for byte. It exits 1 and names each file that differs. Refreshing any input is a
maintainer action: collect the raw records per each comparison's README, then rewrite the tables and
the known result with the same command:
